r1-observability-1.summary: Ledger-service and payments-api experienced severe error rate spikes starting at 13:52 and 13:53 on 2026-10-03 due to ledger-db running out of disk space, causing ledger write failures and marking payments as PENDING for retry.

findings.statement: ledger-service error rate and p99 latency spiked starting at 2026-10-03T13:52:00+00:00.
ledger-service began logging PostgreSQL storage exhaustion errors ('No space left on device') during ledger inserts at 2026-10-03T13:52:00+00:00.
payments-api error rate rose starting at 2026-10-03T13:53:00+00:00.
payments-api began failing ledger writes and marking payments as PENDING for retry starting at 2026-10-03T13:53:03+00:00.

open_questions: What specific table, index, or logs consumed all available disk space on ledger-db?

r1-dependency-2.summary: Retrieved service dependency topology and deployment records around INC-02. Identified four changes in the window up to 7 days back, including a kyc-service deploy right at the reported incident onset (14:00) and a credential rotation config change on payments-api earlier in the day.

findings.statement: payments-api configuration credentials were rotated at 2026-10-03T01:43:00+00:00 (chg-7351).
market-data-service v1.25.0 routine release occurred at 2026-10-03T12:07:00+00:00 (chg-7687).
portfolio-service v6.11.0 routine release occurred at 2026-10-03T12:29:00+00:00 (chg-7952).
kyc-service deployed v5.2.0 (retry Aadhaar e-sign on vendor timeouts) at 2026-10-03T14:00:00+00:00 (chg-9369), matching the reported onset time of payments getting stuck in PENDING.
payments-api depends synchronously on ledger-service, upi-gateway, fraud-service, and redis-cache, and asynchronously on event-bus.
kyc-service depends synchronously on kyc-vendor and user-db.

Although kyc-service deployed right at the incident onset, dependency paths show payments-api and ledger-service are distinct from kyc-service, meaning the kyc-service deploy may be coincidental unless invoked via mobile-bff or upstream workflows.

open_questions: Are payments triggered directly via mobile-bff or do they interact with kyc-service flows prior to hitting payments-api?
What specific metrics and logs show anomalies on ledger-service and payments-api after 14:00?

r2-observability-1.summary: ledger-db experienced disk space exhaustion starting at 13:19 UTC, reaching 100% saturation and causing database write failures with 'No space left on device' errors from 13:52 UTC onwards, which directly led to payments failing and staying PENDING.

findings.statement: metric:ledger-db:disk_used_pct showed an anomaly starting at 13:19 UTC, climbing to 100% saturation at 13:59 UTC.
ledger-db logged 'No space left on device' errors starting at 13:52:08 UTC.
ledger-service error rate and latency anomalies began at 13:52 UTC due to ledger-db storage exhaustion.
payments-api error rate spiked at 13:53 UTC because ledger writes failed, marking payments as PENDING for retry.
The kyc-service deploy at 14:00 UTC occurred after the storage exhaustion and error symptoms had already started.

open_questions: What specific table or file caused the rapid disk consumption on ledger-db?

hypotheses.title: Ledger Database Storage Exhaustion
hypotheses.mechanism: The persistent storage volume attached to ledger-db filled up completely, reaching 100% saturation at 13:59 UTC (with disk usage anomalies starting at 13:19 UTC), causing PostgreSQL to fail all write operations with 'No space left on device' errors starting at 13:52 UTC. This caused ledger-service inserts to fail, which in turn caused payments-api to fail ledger writes and mark payments as PENDING for retry starting at 13:53 UTC.

supporting.note: Shows disk usage anomaly starting at 13:19 UTC, reaching 100% saturation at 13:59 UTC.
Shows ledger-db logging 'could not extend file... No space left on device' starting at 13:52:08 UTC.
Shows error rate spiking sharply starting at 13:52 UTC.
Shows p99 latency spiking starting at 13:52 UTC.
Logs PostgreSQL storage exhaustion during ledger inserts starting at 13:52 UTC.
Shows payments-api error rate rising starting at 13:53 UTC.
Shows payments-api failing ledger writes and marking payments as PENDING starting at 13:53 UTC.
Establishes dependency of ledger-service on ledger-db.

assumptions: The underlying storage volume reached its provisioned disk quota due to accumulated transaction logs or data growth over time.

hypotheses.title: KYC Service Deployment Triggering Downstream Database Bloat
hypotheses.mechanism: The deployment of kyc-service v5.2.0 at 14:00 introduced a regression that flooded ledger-db or shared storage with heavy database activity, exhausting disk space.

supporting.note: kyc-service deployed right around the reported time payments got stuck.

contradicting.note: Disk usage anomaly on ledger-db started at 13:19, and disk saturation/write errors started at 13:52, which are prior to the kyc-service deployment at 14:00.
Storage exhaustion errors started at 13:52, which is 8 minutes before the kyc-service deployment at 14:00.
Ledger-service anomaly started at 13:52, preceding the kyc-service deployment.

assumptions: The kyc-service deployment caused database storage exhaustion despite occurring after the symptoms had already started.

hypotheses.reasoning_summary: Addressing the Critic's note, we have now incorporated the explicit metrics and logs for ledger-db (metric:ledger-db:disk_used_pct showing disk usage climbing from 13:19 UTC to 100% saturation at 13:59 UTC, and log-00706 showing explicit 'No space left on device' errors directly from ledger-db at 13:52:08 UTC). Symptom onset is firmly established at 2026-10-03T13:52:00+00:00. The kyc-service deployment (chg-9369) at 14:00 UTC occurred after the storage exhaustion and error symptoms were already well underway, completely ruling it out. H1 is conclusively the root cause.
